key_insight: Deep learning–reconstructed accelerated whole-body DWI cut scan time by 37% while preserving image quality and lesion ADC measurements in metastatic prostate cancer.
clinical_relevance: This suggests faster metastatic prostate cancer WB-MRI may be feasible without sacrificing the quantitative diffusion information used for staging and treatment assessment.
method: Prospective single-centre study at 1.5T with standard-of-care WB-MRI.
Cohort 1 (n=10): radiologists compared image quality across 4 anatomical stations using a 4-point Likert scale.
Cohort 2 (n=20): ADC values from hypercellular bone metastases were compared between standard and accelerated DL DWI.
evidence_signal: Radiologists rated both protocols as good-to-excellent, and ADC values showed no significant difference between standard and accelerated DL reconstruction on Bland-Altman analysis.
watch_item: Small single-centre cohorts and research-based DL reconstruction mean broader validation is needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: Evaluation of accelerated whole-body diffusion weighted imaging with deep learning reconstruction in patients with metastatic prostate cancer: assessment of image quality and ADC estimates.
